content: 1. These recommendations should be read alongside the accompanying notes. For individuals who are behind schedule or starting vaccinations late, catch-up vaccinations should be administered at the earliest opportunity as indicated by the green bars. To determine the minimum intervals between doses, refer to the catch-up schedule. 2. School entry and adolescent vaccine age groups are highlighted in gray. The provided schedules outline catch-up vaccination protocols and minimum intervals between doses for children whose vaccinations have been delayed. Vaccine series do not need to be restarted, regardless of the time elapsed between doses. Use the section appropriate for the child’s age and always consult this in conjunction with the notes. 3. For routine vaccination, doses are typically administered at 2, 4, 6, and 15–18 months, with a booster at 4–6 years. Dose 4 may be given as early as 12 months of age if at least 6 months have passed since dose 3. 4. Retrospectively, a fourth dose administered as early as 12 months may be counted if at least 4 months have passed since dose 3. Dose 5 is not necessary if dose 4 was administered at age 4 years or older and at least 6 months after dose 3. 5. For Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccination, the minimum age is 6 weeks. Routine vaccination includes a 4-dose series (ActHIB, Hiberix, or Pentacel) at 2, 4, 6, and 12–15 months, or a 3-dose series (PedvaxHIB) at 2, 4, and 12–15 months. 6. For catch-up Hib vaccination: If dose 1 is given at 7–11 months, administer dose 2 at least 4 weeks later and dose 3 (final dose) at 12–15 months or 8 weeks after dose 2, whichever is later. If dose 1 is given at 12–14 months, administer dose 2 (final dose) at least 8 weeks after dose 1. If dose 1 is given before 12 months and dose 2 before 15 months, administer dose 3 (final dose) 8 weeks after dose 2. Individuals who received 1 dose at age 12 months or older should receive dose 2 at least 6 months after dose 1. 7. Adolescents aged 18 years and older may receive the combined Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B vaccine (Twinrix®) as a 3-dose series (0, 1, and 6 months) or a 4-dose series (0, 7, and 21–30 days, followed by a dose at 12 months). 8. For international travel: Infants aged 6–11 months should receive 1 dose before departure and be revaccinated with 2 doses (separated by at least 6 months) between 12 and 23 months of age. Unvaccinated individuals aged 12 months and older should receive dose 1 as soon as travel is considered. 9. For Hepatitis B vaccination, the minimum age is birth. If the mother is HBsAg-negative, administer 1 dose within 24 hours of birth for all medically stable infants weighing ≥2,000 grams. For infants <2,000 grams, administer 1 dose at chronological age 1 month or at hospital discharge. If the mother is HBsAg-positive, administer HepB vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within 12 hours of birth, regardless of birth weight. Infants <2,000 grams should receive 3 additional doses (total of 4 doses) starting at age 1 month. Test for HBsAg and anti-HBs at age 9–12 months. If the mother’s HBsAg status is unknown, administer HepB vaccine within 12 hours of birth. For infants <2,000 grams, also administer HBIG within 12 hours of birth. Determine the mother’s HBsAg status as soon as possible. If the mother is HBsAg-positive, administer HBIG to infants ≥2,000 grams as soon as possible, but no later than 7 days of age. 10. For Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, the minimum age is 9 years. Routine vaccination is recommended at age 11–12 years (can start at age 9) and catch-up vaccination is recommended for all individuals through age 18 years if not adequately vaccinated. For individuals aged 9–14 years at initial vaccination, a 2-dose series is given at 0 and 6–12 months (minimum interval: 5 months). For individuals aged 15 years or older at initial vaccination, a 3-dose series is given at 0, 1–2 months, and 6 months (minimum intervals: dose 1 to dose 2: 4 weeks; dose 2 to dose 3: 12 weeks; dose 1 to dose 3: 5 months). 11. For Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) vaccination, the minimum age is 12 months for routine vaccination. A 2-dose series is given at 12–15 months and 4–6 years. Dose 2 may be administered as early as 4 weeks after dose 1. For unvaccinated children and adolescents, a 2-dose series is given at least 4 weeks apart. 12. For Rotavirus vaccination, the minimum age is 6 weeks. Rotarix is a 2-dose series at 2 and 4 months. RotaTeq is a 3-dose series at 2, 4, and 6 months. If any dose in the series is either RotaTeq or unknown, default to a 3-dose series. Do not start the series on or after age 15 weeks, 0 days. The maximum age for the final dose is 8 months, 0 days. 13. For Tetanus, Diphtheria, and Pertussis (Tdap) vaccination, the minimum age is 11 years for routine vaccination and 7 years for catch-up vaccination. Adolescents aged 11–12 years should receive 1 dose of Tdap. Pregnant individuals should receive 1 dose of Tdap during each pregnancy, preferably between gestational weeks 27–36. Adolescents aged 13–18 years who have not received Tdap should receive 1 dose, followed by Td or Tdap boosters every 10 years. For individuals aged 7–18 years not fully vaccinated with DTaP, administer 1 dose of Tdap as part of the catch-up series (preferably the first dose). If additional doses are needed, use Td or Tdap.
